chapter: Chicago and New York with Louis Armstrong, 1925-30
title: Filling in for Ellington at the Audubon Theatre
summary: In New York the band first opened at the Savoy, then took Duke's place at the Audubon Theatre in the Bronx, where Louis's St. Louis Blues high notes made the pit orchestra stand up.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Where did you play in New York?

Well we first opened at the Savoy here in New York City. Because I sent Marge a telegram saying, breaking Savoy up. Then we got a job to play in Duke's place at the Audobon Theater. And that's when they had the big band in the pit and Louis played the 'St. Louis Blues and hit them high ones. And when we looked down, the band was standing up in the pit.
They never heard it, a guy play like that before. You know, and they must have had about twenty or twenty five pieces in the pit at this band. Because we had to fill in for Duke Ellington.
On Stage?
On stage.
Where was the Audubon Theater?
Up in the Bronx.
In the Bronx.
Way up in the Bronx. That's where Malcolm X was killed. At the Audubon. It was still going.
There's an Audubon sort of ballroom place.
That's the same one.
Yes.
I think they remodeled it, but it was the same Audubon. And they turned it into a ballroom.
I think it was the Rollins because this woman, Hill, she was one of the singers...... ....
No. Was it Letha
Letha Hill.
(Letha)(Letha) Hill, yes.
Yes, Letha Hill.
LEITHA, I know how to spell that.

Henry used to dance with a dummy. He was a good looking, handsome cat. He looked like Buddy Rogers used to look, you know. And he used to do a dance with this dummy woman, you know. Because all that was Duke Ellington's town. And they had a couple of tap dancers. Because it happened so quick. See, we had to just hurry. Rehearse and all that stuff.
So in other words you had a pit band, but you were on stage?
Yes. We were on the stage.
Yes, I see.
Because that's where Duke was, on the stage. But they had a big pit band. A lot of violins and everything.
And Louis really astonished them?
And Louis played the St. Louis Blues that's when he was hitting those high notes. Chops was real good.
And the band played for Louis. They played for Louis. They, that band, they were not
trying to feature themselves. None of them. They were just, they adored Louis. Honest, They just, they were playing for Louis.
